title: ALMA Reveals the Anatomy of the mm-sized Dust and Molecular Gas in the HD 97048 Disk
question: What are the spatial distributions of the mm-sized dust and CO gas in the HD 97048 disk, and does the disk have a cavity and substructure?

data.angular_resolution: 0.88x0.52 arcsec (302 GHz), 0.69x0.43 arcsec (346 GHz) Briggs; superuniform 0.73x0.40 and 0.61x0.36

evidence.quote: The authors find that the SED and brightness profile are best fit with a dust cavity 34 ± 4 au in radius

recipe.method: CLEAN with Briggs (robust 0.5) and superuniform weighting at 302 and 346 GHz
uvmodelfit with elliptical disk on continuum visibilities

assumptions: kappa = 5 cm2/g, T_dust = 30 K, D = 160 pc, optically thin

recipe.goal: Fit radial intensity profile in visibility domain
recipe.method: MCMC fit of sum of Gaussians modulated by cosines to binned, deprojected real visibilities, adding components until residuals stop improving
key_parameters: 10 au radial grid; priors uniform within ≲500 au and ≲500 kλ; flux normal with 10% (302 GHz) and 15% (346 GHz) sigma

recipe.goal: CO imaging, source velocity and disk radius
